## Why it matters internationally

Thermomat is important not only as a laboratory actor in infrared
emissometry, but also as a **builder of community infrastructure**. It
organized IR-EMPOWER as a workshop devoted specifically to infrared
emissivity measurement techniques and protocols, and its environment has
developed **EKHI**, a structured open database for optical and radiative
properties (recent *Scientific Data* / Nature publication). Laboratories
that both measure *and* curate data help transform a fragmented literature
into a reusable scientific resource — which makes Thermomat especially
relevant as a node of community formation, data stewardship, and
methodological convergence.

## Scope of activity

### Relevant units

- **Thermomat — Thermophysical Properties of Materials Research Group
  (UPV/EHU)** — infrared emissometry, radiative-property characterization,
  and development of measurement instrumentation.
- **EKHI — open database of optical and thermal radiative properties for
  solid materials** — supports interactive querying and visualization of
  emittance, reflectance, transmittance, and absorptance records, with a
  FAIR-compliant data structure.

### Radiative properties measured / curated

Emittance · reflectance · transmittance · absorptance · related thermo-optical
and radiative quantities.

### Capability envelope

- **Methodology:** in-house modular high-performance infrared emissometer
  presented at IR-EMPOWER; FAIR-compliant data structure and workflows;
  community-facing instrumentation development.

### Signature infrastructure

- **Modular high-performance infrared emissometer** — in-house
  instrumentation presented at IR-EMPOWER.
- **EKHI** — open database of optical and thermal radiative properties
  for solid materials, backed by a *Scientific Data* (Nature) publication.
  EKHI supports interactive querying and visualization of emittance,
  reflectance, transmittance, and absorptance records.

### Application domains

- Community data stewardship for radiative properties
- FAIR reuse of emissivity and reflectance data
- Methodological convergence across the European emissivity community
- Open infrastructure for radiative-property research

## IR-EMPOWER contributions

- **Organizer of the IR-EMPOWER workshop**.
- Presentation of a **modular high-performance infrared emissometer**.
- Presentation of an **open community of radiative properties** built around
  EKHI.

## Why Thermomat is a reference pole

A working community in radiative-property science needs three things: people
who measure, people who reason, and infrastructure that outlives any single
project. Thermomat works on all three axes at once — running its own
instrumentation, co-organizing the IR-EMPOWER workshop that brings the
European community together, and maintaining EKHI as a durable open-data
backbone. Few groups in the field combine all three.
